source_text:
∆ειλὸς στρατιώτης
ἐκλύει πολεμιστῶν χεῖρας καὶ ἀμελὴς μοναχὸς χαυνοῖ προθυμίαν ἀδελφῶν. Σμῆνος μελισσῶν ἐργάζεται κηρίον καὶ σύστημα ἀδελφῶν βασιλείαν οὐρανῶν. Σάλπιγξ διεγείρει προθυμίαν πολεμιστῶν καὶ μαθητῶν σπουδὴν διδασκαλία πρακτικῆς ἀρετῆς. Ὅπλισον †δακτύλων λόγοις, ἡγούμενε, σοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ θωράκισον ἐπαγγελίαις τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν· φράξον θυρεῷ πίστεως ἄθλοις καὶ περικνήμισον ἐλπίδι τῇ εἰς τὸν θεόν· †κήνησον τοὺς πόδας ἐν εὐαγγελικοῖς μαθήμασι καὶ ζῶσον τὴν ὀσφὺν σωφροσύνης λόγοις· δὸς μάχαιραν εἰς τὴν χεῖρα κατὰ τῶν παθῶν ὀξύτατον θυμὸν καὶ ἀντίταξον φάλαγγα παθῶν ἡδονῇ.
thought_title: Arming the Brothers for Spiritual Combat
orientation: Evagrius continues his direct address to the monastic leader, now commanding him to equip his brothers with spiritual armor and weapons for the fight against the passions.
pass_a_gloss: A cowardly soldier loosens [the] hands of warriors, and a careless monk slackens [the] eagerness of brothers. A swarm of bees works [a] honeycomb, and a company of brothers [works] [the] kingdom of heaven. A trumpet rouses [the] eagerness of warriors, and teaching of active virtue [rouses] [the] zeal of disciples. Arm with words of your fingers, leader, your brothers, and breastplate [them] with promises of the coming good things; fence [them] with [the] shield of faith [and] with contests, and put greaves on [them] with hope in God; move [their] feet in evangelical lessons, and gird [their] loins with words of self-control; give [a] sword into [their] hand against the passions, [a] very sharp zeal, and set against them [a] phalanx of passions with pleasure.

choices.why: The phrase is odd but literal; 'words of fingers' likely means written words or words counted on fingers, and the literal rendering preserves the strangeness for the reader.
rejected: Arm with the words of the fingers

choices.english: put on them the breastplate of the promises of good things to come
choices.why: The verb θωρακίζω means to equip with a breastplate; 'promises of good things to come' keeps the future orientation of μελλόντων.
rejected: breastplate them with promises of future goods
armor them with the promises of coming blessings

choices.english: Fence them with the shield of faith and with contests
choices.why: φράσσω means to fence or hedge around; 'shield of faith' echoes Ephesians 6:16, and 'contests' (ἄθλοις) is kept as a second instrument of defense.
rejected: hedge them with the shield of faith by contests
fence them in with the shield of faith and struggles

choices.why: θυμός here is the spirited part of the soul used as a weapon against the passions; 'very sharp anger' preserves the superlative and the martial image.

choices.english: set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure
choices.why: The syntax is compressed; the leader is to set a phalanx against the passions, using pleasure as the opposing force. The literal rendering keeps the ambiguity of the dative ἡδονῇ.
rejected: oppose the phalanx of passions with pleasure
set against the passions a phalanx by pleasure

pass_b_english: A cowardly soldier makes the hands of warriors go slack, and a careless monk drains the eagerness of his brothers. A swarm of bees produces a honeycomb, and a community of brothers produces the kingdom of heaven. A trumpet rouses the eagerness of warriors, and teaching in active virtue rouses the zeal of disciples. Arm your brothers, leader, with words [the Greek here is corrupt: "of fingers"], and put on them the breastplate of the promises of good things to come. Fence them with the shield of faith in struggles, and put greaves on them with hope in God. Shoe their feet [the printed verb is corrupt; "shoe" is a conjecture] with the lessons of the gospel, and gird their loins with words of self-control. Put into their hand the sharpest anger as a sword against the passions, and set a phalanx of the passions against pleasure.
notes: The source has †δακτύλων and †κήνησον marked with obeli, indicating textual uncertainty or damage. The gloss renders them as they stand: 'of fingers' and 'move'.

problems.why: δακτύλων is genitive plural, likely 'of the fingers' but context suggests 'ten' (δάκτυλοι as numerical). 'Words of fingers' is absurd; should be 'ten words' or 'decalogue' (the Ten Commandments).
problems.fix: Arm your brothers, leader, with the ten words

problems.why: κήνησον is corrupt/unusual; likely κίνησον 'set in motion' but context of arming suggests 'shod' (cf. Eph 6:15). The † indicates textual problem; 'set in motion' misses the arming metaphor.
problems.fix: Shod their feet with the lessons of the gospel

problems.quote: set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure
problems.why: Agency reversed: the leader should set the phalanx of passions against pleasure, not set passions against disciples with pleasure. ἡδονῇ is dative of opposition (pleasure as enemy), not instrument.
problems.fix: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure

problems.quote: Fence them with the shield of faith and with contests
problems.why: ἄθλοις is dative plural of ἆθλος 'contest' but here likely means 'prizes' or 'victories'; more importantly, it goes with θυρεῷ—'shield of faith in contests' or 'shield of faith's struggles'. Current English makes contests separate from shield.
problems.fix: Fence them with the shield of faith in struggles
problems.ruling: ἄθλοις likely modifies θυρεῷ πίστεως; English separates 'contests' from shield, misleading reader on syntax and meaning.

edits.old: Set their feet in motion with the lessons of the gospel
edits.new: Shod their feet with the lessons of the gospel

edits.old: set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure
edits.new: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure

edits.old: Fence them with the shield of faith and with contests
edits.new: Fence them with the shield of faith in struggles

fixed: words of fingers: corrected to 'the ten words'
Set their feet in motion: corrected to 'Shod their feet'
set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure: corrected to 'set a phalanx of passions against pleasure'
Fence them with the shield of faith and with contests: corrected to 'Fence them with the shield of faith in struggles'

problems.why: δακτύλων means 'fingers', not 'ten'; 'ten words' is a wild guess or corruption misread.

problems.quote: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure
problems.why: English says passions oppose pleasure, but source says set a phalanx against the passions, with pleasure as dative (instrument or accompaniment unclear). ἡδονῇ is likely 'with pleasure' as ally or 'for pleasure', not 'against pleasure'.
problems.fix: set a phalanx of passions against [them] with pleasure
problems.ruling: ἀντίταξον φάλαγγα παθῶν ἡδονῇ: phalanx of passions set against pleasure, not passions opposing pleasure

edits.old: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure
edits.new: set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure

fixed: The first problem is real: δακτύλων means 'fingers', so 'ten words' is a mistranslation. Replaced with 'words of your fingers'.
The second problem is real: the source says to set a phalanx against the passions, with pleasure as dative. Replaced with 'set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure'.

problems.why: δακτύλων is genitive plural, likely 'of the fingers' or 'ten'; context suggests 'ten words' (Decalogue), not 'your fingers'.
problems.fix: Arm your brothers, leader, with the words of the ten commandments

problems.quote: set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure
problems.why: ἡδονῇ is dative of means/instrument, not 'with pleasure' as ally; sense is 'set a phalanx of passions against pleasure' or 'oppose pleasure with a phalanx of passions'.
problems.fix: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure

edits.old: Arm your brothers, leader, with words of your fingers
edits.new: Arm your brothers, leader, with the words of the ten commandments

edits.old: set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure
edits.new: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure

problems.why: Single role called by six different titles; reader may not see unity.
problems.fix: Add note: 'leader' = teacher = shepherd = pilot = general = physician.

problems.why: Those led are called disciples, brothers, soldiers, monks interchangeably.
problems.fix: Note: all terms refer to community members under guidance.

problems.why: Same Greek term? 'Active virtue' vs 'virtuous practice' may confuse.

problems.quote: Arm your brothers, leader, with the words of the ten commandments
problems.why: Direct address to 'leader' begins here without signal; prior sections were third-person.
problems.fix: Mark shift to imperative address to the leader.

problems.quote: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure
problems.why: Passions are normally enemies to be defeated, not allies arrayed against pleasure.
problems.fix: Verify Greek: may mean 'array the brothers' passions' or 'passions' as suffering endured.

problems.quote: put into their hand a very sharp anger as a sword against the passions
problems.why: Anger as spiritual weapon contradicts earlier rejection of anger in correction (u01-rem-mid).
problems.fix: Check Greek 'orge': may mean 'zeal' or 'indignation' at sin, not personal anger.

problems.quote: Arm your brothers, leader, with the words of the ten commandments, and put on them the breastplate of the promises of good things to come
problems.why: Ephesians 6:14 has 'breastplate of righteousness,' not 'promises of good things to come.'
problems.fix: Note as free adaptation, not direct citation.

problems.quote: careless monk drains the eagerness of his brothers
problems.why: Same fault type applied to different labels; reader may think monk and brother are distinct categories here.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, or clarify the distinction if intended.

problems.quote: set a phalanx of passions against pleasure
problems.why: 'Passions' deployed as a military formation against pleasure seems contradictory to Evagrian theology where passions are the enemy.
problems.fix: Check Greek; may mean 'virtues' or 'disciplined forces,' not 'passions.'

problems.quote: Arm your brothers, leader, with the words of the ten commandments
problems.why: Sudden direct address to 'leader' shifts from aphoristic description to imperative instruction without clear signal.
problems.fix: Mark the shift from descriptive to imperative mode, or note the treatise alternates styles.

edits.new: Arm your brothers, leader, with words of your fingers

edits.old: Put into their hand a very sharp anger as a sword against the passions
edits.new: Put into their hand a very sharp zeal as a sword against the passions

edits.old: and set a phalanx of passions against pleasure
edits.new: and set a phalanx of passions against them with pleasure

fixed: The glossary notes about leader, disciple, and active virtue are not translation problems; they are editorial suggestions for the apparatus.
The speaker shift to direct address is already marked in the work brief under voices.
The 'phalanx of passions' issue is a mistranslation and has been corrected.
The 'anger' issue is a mistranslation and has been corrected.
The 'ten commandments' issue is a mistranslation and has been corrected.
The 'careless monk' vs 'brothers' issue is not a translation problem; the source uses different terms deliberately.
